claims.text: Enacted text, PL 118-31 sec. 1687(a), 137 Stat. 621: 'LIMITATION ON USE OF FUNDS FOR CERTAIN UNREPORTED PROGRAMS. (a) Limitation on Availability of Funds.--None of the funds authorized to be appropriated or otherwise made available by this Act may be obligated or expended in support of any activities involving unidentified anomalous phenomena protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitations unless the Secretary of Defense has provided the details of the activity to the appropriate congressional committees and congressional leadership, including for any activities described in a report released by the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office in fiscal year 2024.'

Sec. 1687(b), note '50 USC 3373 note': UAP-related independent research and development funding 'shall not be allowable as indirect expenses for purposes of contracts covered by' DoD Instruction 3204.01 unless the material and information is made available to the appropriate congressional committees and congressional leadership.

Sec. 1687(c) defines 'appropriate congressional committees' as the congressional defense committees plus HPSCI and SSCI, and imports the 50 U.S.C. 3373(n) definition of 'unidentified anomalous phenomena'.

Sec. 1687(a) conditions FY2024 DoD funding of UAP special or restricted access activities on the Secretary of Defense providing details to the congressional defence and intelligence committees and congressional leadership.
Sec. 1687(b), noted as 50 U.S.C. 3373 note, disallows UAP-related independent research and development as an indirect expense on covered contracts unless disclosed to Congress.

desc: Section 1687 is the one enacted provision that reaches at the concealment itself rather than at the paperwork. It bars any funds authorised by the FY2024 NDAA from being obligated or expended 'in support of any activities involving unidentified anomalous phenomena protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitations unless the Secretary of Defense has provided the details of the activity to the appropriate congressional committees and congressional leadership, including for any activities described in a report released by the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office in fiscal year 2024.' Subsection (b), noted as 50 U.S.C. 3373 note, then bars UAP-related independent research and development from being allowable as an indirect expense on covered contracts unless the material and information is made available to those same committees — a direct strike at the mechanism by which contractor-held work can be paid for out of overhead without appearing as a Government programme. Its limitation is structural: it restricts funds 'authorized to be appropriated or otherwise made available by this Act,' meaning the FY2024 Act only. It was not re-enacted in the FY2025 NDAA or the FY2026 NDAA, neither of which contains the phrase 'special access or restricted access'. The statutory bar therefore covered one fiscal year and has now been absent for two.
